transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 10:30 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Dana (Volaris Head ML), Omar (SRE), Priya (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on week 3 of KV/prefix cache pilot. Hitrate plateaued, a cohort shows severe drop-off tied to prompt-template churn and session affinity mismatch. Discussed TTL eviction heuristics, prefix-coalescing adjustments, and an experiment to shard by product vertical. Agreed next steps and owner-level actions.

Topics:
- Current KV and prefix hit curves
- Prompt reuse vs template churn
- Eviction TTL & eviction policy tuning
- Instrumentation/logging to debug cold hits
- Pilot sizing and possible dedicated pool vs hosted fallback

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay, uh thanks everyone for hopping on. we wanted to do a quick lockstep on the kv hit numbers we popped earlier this morning. Leo has the dashboard open, right?
[00:14] Leo: yeah i'm sharing, um so two quick things — overall hit rate for the pilot is 41% across all traffic but when we slice by cohort B (the mobile web flow) it drops to 18% around 2pm window, which is where you reported latency spikes.
[00:29] Dana: right that's the one. we saw a bunch of slow tail calls. at first we assumed rate limiting or cold starts but the VMs looked fine.
[00:39] Omar: and the SRE side, we didn't see CPU or mem pressure, it's mostly token generation time.
[00:46] Leo: exactly, so preliminary root cause is low prefix reuse. the mobile prompts are more templated but the front-end injects session metadata in-line which changes the prefix hash.
[01:02] Priya: can you give an example? our product team did try to compact the prompt but maybe we missed something.
[01:09] Leo: yeah, like the template has a user persona block then a session context json blob. a lot of clients append a session_id and platform string, so the cache key differs even though the actual response intent is identical.
[01:21] Dana: ah, so it's an accidental entropy. we were worried about privacy so we added extra fields to each prompt.
[01:27] Maya: makes sense. two paths: we can suggest a prompt normalization step or use a prefix-coalescing rule in runtime to ignore some low-value tokens when computing KV keys.
[01:38] Dana: prompt normalization would be our preferred approach if it's low touch for our engineers. but we need to understand risk of changing inputs for compliance.
[01:47] Omar: also want to call out that some of these sessions are long-lived, we have drift in persona over time — so baseline TTL of 30 minutes may be too short for some flows.
[01:58] Leo: good point. we ran a TTL sensitivity yesterday: increasing session TTL from 30m to 90m helped cohort A hit rate by about 7 points but didn't move cohort B much.
[02:10] Priya: hmm so cohort B is still not benefiting. is that where coalescing helps?
[02:17] Leo: yes, coalescing + token blacklist for certain keys — e.g., session_id, client_version — raised B's hit to around 33% in a synthetic run but the synthetic didn't have the exact front-end noise.
[02:30] Dana: synthetic runs are fine but we need to be careful — we can't strip fields that are required for audit trails.
[02:36] Maya: noted. Leo, can you outline the experiment plan we discussed?
[02:41] Leo: plan A: deploy a read-only coalescing layer that computes an alternate key, logs original vs coalesced key, and doesn't evict anything; run for 48 hours against 10% of traffic for cohort B. Plan B: client-side prompt normalization library we provide as a hotfix — would require a small client rollout.
[03:00] Dana: i like Plan A to start, gives us data without changing client logic.
[03:05] Omar: plus we need more telemetry — right now logs show only hit/miss counts. can we add diffs: length of prefix, entropy estimate, and top-5 differing tokens?
[03:16] Leo: yes, we can add that in the runtime with minimal perf overhead, we tested microbenchmarks.
[03:22] Priya: also curious about eviction policy. are we using LRU or a time-first policy?
[03:27] Leo: it's a hybrid — LRU with TTL buckets. eviction currently prioritizes TTL then recency. we could try an adaptive eviction that considers token freq.
[03:36] Maya: okay, let's brainstorm tradeoffs — adaptive eviction reduces churn but adds complexity and tune surface. for pilot we should keep it simple: TTL sweep + coalesced-key logging.
[03:49] Dana: agree. what about dedicated pool discussion? we keep hitting contention at peak hours and you flagged a hosted fallback when capacity's tight.
[03:58] Leo: for this pilot, we have a shared host with reserved capacity; dedicated pool bump reduces queuing but increases cost by ~28%. we estimated ROI if hit rate goes from 40% to 55% net token cost drop of ~18%.
[04:13] Omar: 28% cost hike is okay if we get consistent latency and SLOs. need to see numbers after coalescing experiment first.
[04:20] Maya: yep. quick question on privacy/compliance — Dana, any red flags for logging coalesced keys?
[04:27] Dana: we need the logs to be PII-free and encrypted. the coalesced key is a hash of normalized tokens, should be okay but our privacy team needs the schema.
[04:36] Maya: we'll redact any raw session_id and only keep hashed keys, plus we can push logs to your KMS.
[04:41] Dana: good.
[04:43] [05:00] Leo: moving to instrumentation, here's the proposed log line: timestamp, original_key_hash, coalesced_key_hash, prefix_len, entropy_score, top_diff_tokens, cohort_tag. will that work for you?
[05:13] Omar: yes, we'll ingest into our ELK pipeline but please make sure the log volume is reasonable — no per-token logs, aggregate at request-level.
[05:23] Leo: got it, request-level only.
[05:27] Priya: on the prompt side, i'll send the product templates that matter most — three main flows — login assist, triage, and clinical summary.
[05:36] Dana: i'll also include an example of the session metadata we append.
[05:40] Maya: great. timeline — run Plan A for 48 hours starting Monday 2026-06-01 at midnight PT, 10% traffic for cohort B, then analyze. Leo to implement logging and coalescing feature flag by 2026-06-02.
[05:54] Leo: sounds doable. one more thought: we noticed prefix collisions where different prompts hash to same key due to truncation. we could change hashing to include a rolling window of tokens rather than fixed prefix.
[06:06] Dana: would that affect memory footprint?
[06:09] Leo: slight increase in key cardinality but manageable; we can cap with bloom-filter-ish dedupe.
[06:15] Priya: okay if you test that in synthetic and share tradeoffs in the experiment doc.
[06:21] Maya: i'll own the experiment doc and share with Dana's team.
[06:25] Dana: perfect.
[06:27] [07:00] Omar: uh, small ops question — if we increase TTL for some flows, what's the impact on KV storage growth?
[07:35] Leo: for cohort A we tracked storage growth of ~12% with 90m TTL vs 30m. for B, because of low reuse, growth was minimal until coalescing kicks in.
[07:50] Dana: so net cost depends on hit improvement.
[07:53] Maya: exactly.
[07:55] Priya: are there any quick wins we can do on the product side before the Redwood experiment?
[08:00] Dana: we'll try a small client-side normalization patch for the triage flow and report back in 48h.
[08:06] Maya: awesome.
[08:08] [08:30] Leo: i'll drop the experiment runbook in the pilot folder and include the log schema and dashboards.
[08:40] Maya: and i'll put together an updated pilot pricing addendum with dedicated-pool delta and extension option.
[08:46] Dana: thanks, team.
[08:48] [09:00] (overlapping chatter)
[09:12] Priya: one last thing — should we schedule the benchmark with real traffic next week?
[09:17] Maya: yes let's do Tuesday 2026-06-02 15:00 PT for a 30m window, agreed?
[09:23] Omar: works for us.
[09:24] Dana: works.
[09:26] Maya: ok closing notes: Plan A coalescing read-only flag for 10% cohort B traffic, TTL sweep experiment scoped, logging schema added, customer to share prompts and session examples, Redwood to send pricing. meet again after 48h with results.
[09:42] END

Notes about transcription: occasional partial words and speaker overlaps present; some technical terms spelled as they sounded in transcript (e.g., "kv" vs "K-V").
notes: Pilot week 3 focused on debugging unexpected low hit rate in mobile cohort; agreed on read-only coalescing experiment + TTL sweep; customer to provide prompt samples; follow-up benchmark on 2026-06-02 15:00 PT.
